items.text: We propose SPECTER, a new method to generate document-level embedding of scientiﬁc documents based on pretraining a Transformer language model on a powerful signal of document-level relatedness: the citation graph.
items.why: It introduces SPECTER and its core approach using citation-graph pretraining.
items.plain: We introduce SPECTER, a method that creates vector representations for scientific documents by pretraining a Transformer language model using document citation networks.

items.text: Unlike existing pretrained language models, SPECTER can be easily applied to downstream applications without task-speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning.
items.why: It states a key practical advantage regarding task adaptation.
items.plain: Unlike other pretrained language models, SPECTER can be applied directly to downstream tasks without needing extra task-specific training.

items.text: Additionally, to encourage further research on document-level models, we introduce SCIDOCS, a new evaluation benchmark consisting of seven document-level tasks ranging from citation prediction, to document classiﬁcation and recommendation.
items.why: It introduces the new benchmark suite created in this work.
items.plain: We also present SCIDOCS, a new test suite featuring seven document-level tasks including citation prediction, document classification, and paper recommendation.

items.text: Our system, SPECTER,2 incorporates inter-document context into the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) language models (e.g., SciBERT (Beltagy et al., 2019)) to learn document representations that are effective across a wide-variety of downstream tasks, without the need for any task-speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning of the pretrained language model.
items.why: It summarizes how SPECTER operates across tasks without fine-tuning.
items.plain: SPECTER combines inter-document context into Transformer language models to generate paper representations that work across many tasks without needing task-specific fine-tuning.

items.text: Unlike many prior works, at inference time, our model does not require any citation information.
items.why: It highlights an essential functional capability at inference time.
items.plain: When generating an embedding, the model does not require any citation data for the input document.

items.text: Overall, we observe substantial improvements across all tasks with average performance of 80.0 across all metrics on all tasks which is a 3.1 point absolute improvement over the next-best baseline.
items.why: It gives the overall headline quantitative improvement over baselines.
items.plain: Overall, our model achieved an average performance score of 80.0 across all benchmark tasks and metrics, which is a 3.1-point absolute improvement over the best competing method.

items.text: In a dataset of 4,113 clicks, we found that SPECTER ranker improved clickthrough rate over the baseline by 46.5%, demonstrating its superiority.
items.why: It highlights the real-world deployment result.
items.plain: In an online test measuring 4,113 clicks, the SPECTER recommendation system increased user clickthrough rates by 46.5% compared to the existing system.

items.text: We experiment with ﬁne-tuning SciBERT on our tasks, and ﬁnd this to be generally inferior to using our ﬁxed representations from SPECTER.
items.why: It presents a takeaway comparing fixed SPECTER embeddings to task fine-tuning.
items.plain: Fine-tuning SciBERT directly on specific downstream tasks performed worse than using SPECTER's fixed paper representations.
